scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The manuscript presents a sensible hybrid architecture concept, but the evaluation design carries substantial scientific uncertainty. Testing is limited to a single interferogram without clear spatial cross-validation controls, GNSS/ground-truth validation, or comparison against standard remote sensing deformation pipelines.

deep learning models often struggle to resolve subtle deformation signals from complex phase noise

evidence.excerpt:
Inception-based
multi-scale patch embedding stem and a depthwise-convolutional feed-forward network (DW-FFN) to
inject local inductive bias into the Transformer framework. Experimental results demonstrate that the
proposed architecture achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 97.58% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.966
across 50,854 validation samples. Class-wise evaluation highlights exceptional performance in
identifying high-intensity deformation zones (F1-score} = 0.99). Furthermore, Explainable AI (XAI)
attention mapping confirms that the network effectively suppresses decorrelation noise and
atmospheric phase screens by prioritizing physically consistent phase gradients. These findings
demonstrate that embedding multi-scale convolutional priors within Vision Transformers provides a
robust, interpretable mechanism for rapid geodetic assessment and earthquake monitoring.

evidence.excerpt:
The study focuses on the 6.1 Mw Sındırgı earthquake located in the Balıkesir province of western
Türkiye. This region is governed by an active extensional and strike-slip tectonic regime within the
Western Anatolian Extensional Province (Shafapourtehrany et al., 2023). The seismic event induced
significant Line-of-Sight (LOS) surface displacements across complex topographic terrain, presenting a
challenging environment for evaluating model robustness against spatial decorrelation and atmospheric
phase screens (Xie, 2025). The geographical context and the main fault systems of the study area are
illustrated in Fig. 1.

acquisitions captured in Interferometric Wide (IW) Single Look Complex (SLC) mode. The interferometric
pair covers the pre-seismic and post-seismic periods of the Sındırgı event. Topographic phase
components were removed using the 30-meter Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) DEM, and
adaptive phase filtering was applied to optimize coherence. The resulting wrapped phase interferogram,
highlighting the seismic deformation fringes, is presented in Fig. 2.

evidence.excerpt:
To create a supervised learning environment, the interferogram was labeled into discrete classes using a
combined approach of statistical estimation and expert validation.
Ground Truth Generation: Initially, the Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC) algorithm was used to
categorize the phase values (Li et al., 2023). These results were then manually refined based on the
technical legends to ensure the accuracy of the training labels.
Displacement Scaling: The labeling process was governed by the physical parameters of the C-band SAR
signal. As shown in the technical legends (Fig. 3), the dataset is scaled to reflect a Line-of-Sight (LOS)
displacement range of approximately − 0.03 m (subsidence) to + 0.03 m (uplift). In the wrapped phase
domain, each full fringe cycle (-π to + π) corresponds to 2.8 cm of ground movement (Daramola et al.,
2025).

evidence.excerpt:
To address the limitations of standard ViTs, we propose the INRA-Transformer, a hybrid model that
integrates convolutional layers into the Transformer framework. The architecture is composed of three
main components designed to handle the noise and scale complexity of the Sındırgı earthquake dataset:
Inception-Based Patch Embedding (Multi-Scale Stem):Standard ViTs use a single-scale linear
projection to divide the image into patches. However, seismic signals exist at multiple spatial
scales. Our model replaces the linear projection with an Inception-style stem (Zhou et al., 2025). By
using parallel convolutional filters (e.g., 3x3, 5x5, 7x7), the model can capture micro-scale phase
transitions while simultaneously identifying broad deformation trends. This multi-scale approach is
particularly effective at suppressing the chaotic decorrelation noise often found in Sentinel-1A

performance of the proposed INRA-Transformer architecture and compare it with benchmark models.

The quantitative classification performance of the proposed INRA-Transformer architecture was
thoroughly evaluated using the validation dataset derived from the Sentinel-1A DInSAR interferogram.
The primary objective is to differentiate various seismic displacement intensities and stable background
regions across the 6.1 Mw Sındırgı earthquake area. To comprehensively evaluate the pixel-level
classification capability of our hybrid framework, a total of 50,854 validation pixels were analyzed across
five distinct deformation categories.
The confusion matrix obtained from the experimental studies conducted with the proposed method
provides a detailed breakdown of correct and misclassified pixel counts across all classes. The resulting
class-wise distribution and prediction accuracy are visualized in the confusion matrix in Fig. 6.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No independent external physical measurements (e.g., GNSS, leveling, or independent geodetic models) are reported to corroborate the deformation classifications.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pixel classification metrics (OA, AA, Kappa, F1-score) computed against the same pseudo-ground truth labeling scheme on the single event.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss optimized against pseudo-ground truth pixel labels generated from Maximum Likelihood Classification and manual refinement.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of robust deformation mapping and noise suppression across seismic events are evaluated on only one single interferogram event without independent geodetic validation (such as GNSS stations or independent seismic field data). Potential data leakage across spatial patches or adjacent pixels during pixel-level evaluation is unaddressed.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted entirely on 50,854 validation pixels from a single earthquake interferogram whose pseudo-ground truth was generated by Maximum Likelihood Classification followed by manual refinement. Only a single standard ViT baseline is compared; established DInSAR unwrapping/deformation models or strong CNN benchmarks are omitted.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No independent external physical measurements (such as continuous GNSS station displacements, leveling surveys, or external seismic fault models) are evaluated to corroborate the deformation classifications.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pixel classification metrics (OA, AA, Kappa, F1-score) calculated against the same pseudo-ground truth labeling scheme on the single event.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss optimized against pseudo-ground truth pixel labels generated from Maximum Likelihood Classification and manual refinement.

primary.limitations: The study relies on a single seismic event and satellite acquisition pair. Ground truth relies partially on automated statistical classification (MLC) rather than independent in-situ physical measurements.
primary.method_assessment: The architecture combines multi-scale convolutional operations with standard self-attention mechanisms and depthwise-separable FFN blocks. However, the exact data splitting protocol (e.g., random pixel splitting vs. spatially disjoint split), dataset size details, training hyperparameters, and baseline implementation details are minimally described.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a sensible hybrid architecture concept, but the evaluation design carries substantial scientific uncertainty. Testing is limited to a single interferogram without clear spatial cross-validation controls, GNSS/ground-truth validation, or comparison against standard remote sensing deformation pipelines.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes INRA-Transformer, a hybrid Vision Transformer incorporating an Inception-based multi-scale patch embedding stem and a depthwise-convolutional feed-forward network to classify seismic surface deformation zones from Sentinel-1A DInSAR interferograms of the 6.1 Mw Sındırgı earthquake.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a sensible hybrid architecture concept, but the evaluation design carries substantial scientific uncertainty. Testing is limited to a single interferogram without clear spatial cross-validation controls, GNSS/ground-truth validation, or comparison against standard remote sensing deformation pipelines.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The study relies on a single seismic event and satellite acquisition pair. Ground truth relies partially on automated statistical classification (MLC) rather than independent in-situ physical measurements.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
